abstract: Lean 4 / Mathlib formalization of two results. (1) An explicit lower bound for the linear form Λ = (K + L) log 2 − K log 3: for every K ≥ 2438425051595107335801557824 and every L, Λ cannot satisfy 0 < Λ < 100 · 2^(1 − K/2^68). This new self-contained bound is proved from Mathlib using explicit symmetric multipoint Padé approximants (the z = x(70 − x) kernel of Salikhov and Bouchelaghem–He–Li–Wu) together with an elementary bound on lcm(1, …, n), replacing the use of Rhin's (1987) effective irrationality measure in Collatz cycle arguments. (2) An independent proof of Hercher's (2023) theorem on Collatz m-cycles: assuming Bařina's 2025 computer verification that every integer 1 ≤ k ≤ 2^71 reaches 1 under the Collatz map (passed as an explicit hypothesis), there is no non-trivial cycle of the shortcut Collatz map with m ≤ 91 local minima. Rather than Hercher's finite search and Rhin's (1987) bound, the proof here combines a Raney-type rotation of the cycle, a telescopic lower bound on every local minimum, a 2-adic unimodular reduction, and a kernel-checked chain of continued-fraction steps that forces the number of odd steps past the range of (1). The definitions of the shortcut map and of m-cycles follow Moritz Firsching's formal-conjectures specification. This is an incremental m-cycle certificate plus a formalization; it does not address general cycles or divergent orbits. Both theorems use only propext, Classical.choice and Quot.sound. Four supporting statements are also compared: the trivial cycle 1 → 2 → 1 is a 1-cycle through 1 and through 2, every m-cycle has m ≥ 1, and (under the same hypothesis) every element of a non-trivial cycle exceeds 2^71.
title: Collatz m-cycles for m ≤ 91 (conditional on Bařina's 2^71 check) and an explicit linear-form bound for log 2 and log 3

abstract: A Lean 4 / Mathlib proof of Exoo's lower bound R(5,5) ≥ 43 for the diagonal graph Ramsey number: there is a simple graph on 42 vertices with no clique of size 5 and no independent set of size 5. The proof defines a clique scan on natural-number bit masks, proves that a scan with the result `false` excludes every clique of the given size, and lets the Lean kernel evaluate the scan on one explicit graph and on its complement (`decide +kernel`, no `native_decide`). The statement is the one that the Formal Conjectures repository records as `RamseyNumbers.ramsey_number_five_five_lower_bound`. The value of R(5,5) is open; 43 has been the best known lower bound since 1989.
title: The lower bound R(5,5) ≥ 43: a kernel-checked Ramsey graph on 42 vertices

abstract: Kernel-checked proofs, in Lean 4 + Mathlib, of nine statements about the Lie algebra L of the linear endomorphisms of four-dimensional Minkowski space that are skew-adjoint for the Minkowski form. Main theorem, (6): a real bilinear form B on L satisfies B([Z,X],Y) + B(X,[Z,Y]) = 0 for all X, Y, Z if and only if B(X,Y) = a tr(XY) + b tr(H(X)Y) for exactly one pair of real numbers (a,b); every such form is symmetric. Here tr(XY) is the trace form of L acting on Minkowski space and H is the operator of (4). For a real simple Lie algebra whose complexification is simple the invariant symmetric bilinear forms are the multiples of the Killing form; for a complex simple Lie algebra regarded as a real one they form a plane (Francis-Staite and Leistner, Proposition 4.1). L is of the second kind: it is sl(2,C) regarded as a real Lie algebra ((1), (2)), H is multiplication by -i under that isomorphism ((4)), and tr(H(X)Y) is a second invariant form, not a multiple of the Killing form (Olafsson and Quiroga-Barranco, Remark A.10, where it is, up to a nonzero factor, K(X, J Y)). Read with X as a field strength, tr(XX) and tr(H(X)X) are, up to normalisation, the Maxwell term and the theta term (Tong's names); that reading is not formalized. Statements (1)-(5): sl(2,C), the exponential criterion, the operator H and the complexification; (2) and (4) are the structure behind the second term of (6). (1) On Mathlib's own objects, with nothing carried: Mathlib's so' (Fin 1) (Fin 3) R is isomorphic, as a real Lie algebra, to sl(2,C) (Mathlib's sl (Fin 2) C with scalars restricted to R), by the explicit map X -> -(1/2) sum_k (beta_k + i theta_k) sigma_k, where beta_k and theta_k are the boost and rotation entries of X and sigma_k are the Pauli matrices. (2) On the carried copy of Minkowski space: L has dimension 6; the same map is an isomorphism of real Lie algebras from L onto sl(2,C); the three boost generators and the three rotation generators are in L, the boost along the axis k goes to -(1/2) sigma_k and the rotation in the plane of the two other axes goes to -(i/2) sigma_k. (3) The exponential criterion: a continuous linear endomorphism A is in L if and only if exp(tA) is in the carried type ProperLorentz for every real t; the statement also records that the Minkowski form used for L has the carried minkowskiSquare as its quadratic form. (4) The explicit operator H (the boost along the axis k goes to minus the rotation in the plane of the two other axes, and that rotation goes to the boost) maps L into L, is real-linear there, satisfies H[X,Y] = [X,HY] and H(HX) = -X, and the isomorphism of (2) carries it to multiplication by -i on sl(2,C). (5) The complexification C (x)_R L is isomorphic, as a complex Lie algebra, to sl(2,C) x sl(2,C), and the two maps (1/2)(1 + iH) and (1/2)(1 - iH) are the projections onto the two factors, H being the operator of (4) extended C-linearly. Controls: (7) for the definite diagonal form diag(1,1,1,1) the Lie algebra of skew matrices is isomorphic to so(3) x so(3), for the split form diag(1,1,-1,-1) it is isomorphic to sl(2,R) x sl(2,R), and neither of the two is isomorphic to sl(2,C) as a real Lie algebra; (8) there is a bilinear form on L that is not a tr(XY) + b tr(H(X)Y) for any real a, b; (9) there is a continuous linear endomorphism A with exp(A) in ProperLorentz and A not in L. Numbering as in comparator.json. Statement (1) and part (b) of statement (2) are one isomorphism on two presentations; they are not two results. The Challenge imports Mathlib only. The definitions of Minkowski space and of the Lorentz transformations (Spacetime, minkowskiSquare, ProperLorentz and eight more) are copies carried textually from the public statement of the Yang-Mills release, repository github.com/yang-mills-group/OpenAI-YM-20261028, commit 3456e5e75cf8d4cd558955a5c7638fba2d68f464, file PublicTheory.lean, under the Apache License, Version 2.0; the source file is not imported. Statement (6) is proved from the classification of the linear maps R of L with R[X,Y] = [X,RY], which is the subject of a separate entry in preparation and is not compared here. Audience. Formal developments that use the Lorentz Lie algebra as an object. physlib's lorentzAlgebra is Mathlib's so' (Fin 1) (Fin 3) R, the object of (1); physlib also proves that the complex coefficient tensors with four vector indices invariant under SL(2,C) acting through the Lorentz group are combinations of the three pairings of the metric and the alternating symbol (independence is not proved there). The Yang-Mills release works with the Lorentz Lie algebra of this entry as the predicate tangent (X^T = -theta X theta) on its own 4 x 4 matrix type, splits it into rotations and boosts (tangent_parts), and proves, under its hypothesis Spin.Port, that its Wick-rotated map into operators on field labels respects brackets whenever the first argument is a boost (rank_bracket), in YM/Next/BOUNDARY/Derived.lean; it does not state or use any of the nine statements here, and its matrix type is not the carried Spacetime. The monograph project hairer/humanise-yang-mills proves that invariant bilinear forms on the compact colour algebra are scalar multiples using a positive invariant inner product (manuscript/existence/trace-free-rank.tex, lines 34-51, commit 0f00ae72); (6) shows that on so(3,1), which is simple but has no such inner product, the invariant forms are a two-parameter family. No one at these projects was contacted, and none of them has asked for or endorsed this entry. Literature. This entry formalizes known mathematics; the clauses not found printed are listed below. (1) and (2) are the Lie-algebra form of Spin(3,1) = SL(2,C) (Woit, Quantum Theory, Groups and Representations, sections 40.2 and 40.4; the formula is printed on generators in section 41.2; Olafsson and Quiroga-Barranco, Lemma A.1, state so(3,1) = sl(2,C)_R); (3) is the description of the Lie algebra of a matrix group by its one-parameter subgroups (Hall, arXiv:math-ph/0005032, Definition 3.13; proved there for O(n;k), which includes O(3;1), Chapter 3, section 5.6), stated here for the proper orthochronous subgroup, and (9) is an exercise of that chapter; (4) is the Hodge operator on so(3,1) (Wise, Class. Quantum Grav. 27 (2010) 155010, Appendix); (5) is the splitting of the complexified Lorentz algebra (Woit, section 40.2; Sahlmann and Seeger, Class. Quantum Grav. 41 (2024) 075010, section 2.2.1); (6) is the description of the invariant bilinear forms of a complex simple Lie algebra regarded as a real one (Olafsson and Quiroga-Barranco, Transform. Groups 17 (2012), Remark A.10; Francis-Staite and Leistner, Transform. Groups 26 (2021), Proposition 4.1); parts (a) and (b) of (7) are the companion isomorphisms in the two other signatures (Woit, section 21.2; Olafsson and Quiroga-Barranco, Remark A.2); (8) holds by a count of dimensions (the bilinear forms on L have dimension 36 and the forms of statement 6 are a plane). Not found printed in the sources read: the clause of (4) on multiplication by -i, and parts (c) and (d) of (7); README.md says how each follows from what is printed. Prior formalization, recorded under related_formalizations (search of 2026-11-13): no formalization of a compared statement was found. The counterparts for groups of (1), (2), (5), (7a) and (7b) are in TauCeti, and the homomorphism from SL(2,C) onto the restricted Lorentz group is in physlib; every ingredient of (1) and (2) is in TauCeti and was not found combined there. The equivalence of (3) is proved in TauCeti as a general theorem for the unitary group of a complete normed real algebra with a continuous involution (the form-preservation part of (3) is a case of it, by a reading that was not compiled), for the matrix groups O(n), SO(n), SL(n), SU(n) and the symplectic group, and for the Spin groups; its direction from the algebra to the group is proved for Lorentz matrices in physlib and in OSreconstruction; it was not found with both directions for the Lorentz group or another indefinite orthogonal group of linear maps. For (6), TauCeti has the uniqueness of invariant forms over an algebraically closed field and physlib the invariant coefficient tensors with four vector indices. For (5), TauCeti has extension of scalars for the skew-adjoint matrices of a Gram matrix and the complexifications of so(n) and su(n); the splitting into sl(2,C) x sl(2,C) was not found. The Hodge operator of Euclidean four-space on matrices is in github.com/openai/math. Not formalized: no covering map from SL(2,C) to ProperLorentz, no Lie group structure, no connectedness statement, no statement that every element of ProperLorentz is an exponential; other dimensions and signatures beyond (7); the identification of L with two-forms; the Killing form; the invariant forms of the complexification. Also proved in the library, not compared: Minkowski space from a number field. For a number field K with exactly two real places and exactly one complex place there is a real-linear equivalence e from Mathlib's mixedSpace K onto Spacetime with minkowskiSquare(e x) = -Tr_{K/Q}(x^2) for every x in K, and conjugation by e is an isomorphism of real Lie algebras onto L from the Lie algebra of the endomorphisms of mixedSpace K that are skew-adjoint for the form that restricts to Tr_{K/Q}(x^2) on K. This is proved in the library of this entry and is not compared.
title: Invariant bilinear forms on the Lorentz Lie algebra so(3,1): the two-parameter family a tr(XY) + b tr(H(X)Y), with sl(2,C), the exponential criterion and the complexification

abstract: Kernel-checked proofs, in Lean 4 + Mathlib, of nine statements about R^n with a diagonal metric eta whose entries are +1 or -1 (every signature). A covector field omega is conformal Killing when it is C^3 and d_i omega_j + d_j omega_i = 2 phi eta_ij for some function phi, and Killing when it is C^3 and d_i omega_j + d_j omega_i = 0. (1) For n >= 3 the conformal Killing fields are exactly the members of an explicit family: translations, rotations (an antisymmetric matrix), the dilation and the special conformal fields. (2) In every dimension the Killing fields are exactly the affine fields a + A x with A antisymmetric. (3) For n >= 3 the conformal Killing fields form a real vector space of finite dimension (n+1)(n+2)/2. (4) In every dimension the Killing fields form a real vector space of finite dimension n(n+1)/2. (5) A control for the hypothesis n >= 3 of (1): in the Euclidean plane there is a conformal Killing field that is not a member of the family for any values of its parameters, the matrix being any real matrix, antisymmetric or not (the witness in the proof is the real and imaginary parts of z^3). Statements (6)-(9) are statements about conserved currents: they say which fields give conserved currents. (6) If a tensor field T and a covector field omega are differentiable at a point x, T(x) is symmetric and the conformal Killing equation holds at x with factor phi, then the current J^i = sum_j T^ij omega_j satisfies div J = (div T) . omega + phi tr_eta T at x. (7) A C^3 field is conformal Killing if and only if the current of every differentiable, symmetric, divergence-free, eta-trace-free tensor field against it is divergence-free. (8) A C^3 field is Killing if and only if the current of every differentiable, symmetric, divergence-free tensor field against it is divergence-free. (9) For n >= 1 the dilation omega_j = eta_j x_j is conformal Killing and is not Killing. The Challenge imports Mathlib only and carries the definitions its statements use (the partial derivative, the two equations, the family, the two solution spaces as submodules, the divergences, the current and the metric trace), each with its convention. Statements (1)-(4) are classical: (1) and (3) are the classification of the conformal Killing fields of R^{p,q}, p + q >= 3, and the count of their parameters (Schottenloher 2008, Theorem 1.7; Ginsparg 1988, section 1.1), the infinitesimal counterpart of Liouville's theorem on conformal maps; (2) and (4) are the Killing fields of flat space and their number. (6) is the standard identity behind the conserved currents of a trace-free stress tensor, and (5) and (9) are standard examples. In (7) and (8) the direction from the equation to conserved currents is (6); the other direction was not found stated in the sources read for this entry, is elementary (it is proved by testing on constant tensor fields, so it is a pointwise fact of linear algebra) and is not claimed as new. No statement is claimed as a new theorem. Scope: diagonal metrics with entries +1 or -1 (a general constant metric, reached by a linear change of coordinates, is not formalized); C^3 covector fields on all of R^n; the numbers in (3) and (4) are dimensions of real vector spaces, with no Lie bracket and no isomorphism with so(p+1,q+1) stated; the finite conformal maps (Liouville's theorem itself) are not formalized; nothing is said about compactly supported tensor fields in (7) and (8). Prior formalization, recorded under related_formalizations: the identity (6), with its corollary for conserved trace-free tensors, is formalized for n = 4 and signature (1,3), for tensors of tempered distributions, in github.com/openai/math; special cases of the currents are in the Yang-Mills release github.com/yang-mills-group/OpenAI-YM-20261028 and in facebookresearch/atlas-lean, and Killing fields on Riemannian manifolds are in atlas-lean and in TauCetiProject/TauCeti. In a dated search no formalization was found of (1)-(5) or of the direction of (7) and (8) from conserved currents to the equation. Application (cited; no compared statement asserts it): for n = 4 and a Lorentzian signature the spaces of (3) and (4) have dimensions 15 and 10, the infinitesimal conformal symmetries and the infinitesimal isometries of Minkowski space, and (6) is the conservation law for the currents of a conserved symmetric stress tensor against them, trace-free in the conformal case.
title: Conformal Killing and Killing fields of flat pseudo-Euclidean space: classification for n >= 3 in every signature, the two dimension counts, and the divergence of the current of a symmetric tensor field

abstract: Kernel-checked proofs, in Lean 4 + Mathlib, of six statements. An additive map phi between associative rings is a Jordan homomorphism when phi(ab + ba) = phi(a)phi(b) + phi(b)phi(a). (1) A Jordan homomorphism onto a prime ring without 2-torsion is a homomorphism or an anti-homomorphism (phi(ab) = phi(b)phi(a)): Herstein's theorem (1956, Theorem H) in the form Smiley gave it (1957, p. 428), with characteristic 3 admitted; an additive map of rings, no identity assumed. (2) The domain form in every characteristic (Jacobson and Rickart 1950, Theorem 2): an additive map with phi(a^2) = phi(a)^2 and phi(aba) = phi(a)phi(b)phi(a), into a ring without zero divisors, is multiplicative or anti-multiplicative, with no surjectivity and no hypothesis on 2. (3)-(5) Each hypothesis of (1) is needed; each statement asserts that one hypothesis fails, that the others hold, and that the map is neither multiplicative nor anti-multiplicative: (3) from 2x2 into 4x4 integer matrices, not onto, the target prime and without 2-torsion (witness a -> diag(a, a^T)); (4) on pairs of 2x2 integer matrices, onto, the target not prime (witness (a, b) -> (a, b^T)); (5) from F_2 x F_2 onto F_2, a prime ring with 2-torsion (witness (x, y) -> x + y). (6) The theorem in every characteristic (Smiley 1957, Added in proof, p. 429): an additive map with the two identities of (2), onto a prime ring, is a homomorphism or an anti-homomorphism, with no hypothesis on 2; it implies (1), and (5) shows that the Jordan identity alone does not suffice when the ring has 2-torsion. The compared statements add no definition: the identities on the map and the conditions on the target ring are written out as universally quantified statements, the maps are Mathlib's AddMonoidHom, and onto is Function.Surjective. Statements 1, 2 and 6 formalize theorems of the 1950s and statements 3-5 are standard examples; nothing here is a new theorem. The proof of (1) follows the argument written out by Beidar, Bresar and Chebotar (2003, Proposition 3.1), not Smiley's; the proof of (2) is Jacobson and Rickart's; the proof of (6) is Smiley's, through his lemma that a prime ring in which every commutator squares to zero is commutative. Not formalized: the semiprime generalizations. A prior formalization of the case of complex-linear maps between unital complex algebras exists in github.com/openai/math and is recorded under related_formalizations; statements (1) and (6) contain that case. Application (cited; no compared statement asserts it): the self-adjoint elements of an algebra of observables are closed under the symmetrized product and not, in general, under the product; applied to the identity map, (1) says that on a prime ring without 2-torsion the symmetrized product determines the associative product up to reversing the order of the factors.
title: Herstein's theorem on Jordan homomorphisms onto prime rings, in Smiley's form for characteristic different from 2 and in his form for every characteristic, with the Jacobson-Rickart domain theorem and an example for each hypothesis

abstract: Let f(y) be the decimal reversal of the y-th prime (f(1) = 2, f(2) = 3, f(5) = 11, f(11) = 13). OEIS A100475 is the orbit of 1 under f, and its entry asks (Jonathan Vos Post, 2004) whether the orbit of any other positive start ever enters a loop. This project proves that it never does, i.e. the negation of the formal-conjectures statement OeisA100475.conjecture: the number of digits never decreases along an orbit (p_y > y, and a prime never ends in 0), so on a cycle it is a constant D and every cycle element v satisfies p_v < 10^D; for D <= 4 this forces v <= 1229, and a kernel-checked table of the first 1230 primes with an escape-time ranking shows that no cycle stays below 1230; for D >= 5 it contradicts the bound pi'(10^D) < 10^(D-1) on the number of primes below 10^D, proved for D = 5, ..., 8 by Legendre's sieve recursion evaluated by the Lean kernel and for D >= 9 by Chebyshev's bound theta(x) <= x log 4 with the split point 10^(D-2).
title: OEIS A100475: the reverse-prime map never loops

abstract: A Lean 4 formalization of material in a forthcoming manuscript entitled "The Orthogonal Art Gallery Problem is ∃ℝ-complete". A Lean 4 and Mathlib proof, for an explicit single-tape Turing machine model, that deciding whether an orthogonal simple polygon (every edge horizontal or vertical) with rational corners can be guarded by g points of its boundary, which together must see the whole closed polygon (the boundary-point variant), is ∃ℝ-complete under polynomial-time many-one reductions. The orthogonal point-point and point-boundary variants are the subject of the author's earlier entry PALOMAR-2026-11-01-000004 v1, whose definitions this entry reuses unchanged. For general polygons the boundary-point variant is treated by Abrahamsen, Adamaszek and Miltzow (J. ACM 2021); orthogonal polygons are not. The hardness proof is a new construction: the ETR-INV instance is compiled to rows of fourteen relation profiles, and the polygon is a hub with one floor slot per variable and one door per row, behind each of which hangs an orthogonal wing (a staircase corridor ending in an arithmetic room) whose boundary guards copy the slot values through the door and enforce the row relation. Its finite visibility facts are kernel-checked certificates on the wing charts, parametric in the size and value parameters. The proofs use only the axioms propext, Classical.choice and Quot.sound.
title: The orthogonal boundary-point art gallery problem is ∃ℝ-complete, in Lean 4

abstract: Kernel-checked proofs, in Lean 4 + Mathlib, of six statements. Write ||x|| = |x - round x| for the distance from a real number to the nearest integer, and let rho be the plastic number, the real root of x^3 = x + 1 and the smallest Pisot number (Siegel 1944). Convergence of sum_{n >= 1} ||theta^n||^2 for a Pisot number theta is elementary, and Pisot (1938) proved the converse; neither gives the value. (1) For every real rho with rho^3 = rho + 1, sum_{n >= 1} ||rho^n||^2 = rho (as a HasSum). (2) The tsum form of (1). (3) For every complex alpha != rho with alpha^3 = alpha + 1 (one of the two conjugates inside the unit disc), sum_{n >= 0} (alpha^(2n) + conj(alpha)^(2n)) = rho: the even-power trace of the hidden pair is the generator, the mechanism behind (1), because x^3 - x - 1 = (x - 1) x (x + 1) - 1 makes the resolvent trace sum_{roots} 1/(1 - r^2) vanish. (4) For a real theta, a complex alpha with ||alpha|| < 1, and integers a, b, c that are the elementary symmetric functions of (theta, alpha, conj alpha): sum_{n >= 1} (S_n - theta^n)^2 = Re(geo alpha), where S_n are the Newton power sums of x^3 - a x^2 + b x - c and geo alpha = alpha^2/(1 - alpha^2) + conj(alpha)^2/(1 - conj(alpha)^2) + 2 alpha conj(alpha)/(1 - alpha conj(alpha)). (5) Under the same hypotheses, for every N with ||alpha||^N < 1/4, sum_{n >= 1} ||theta^n||^2 = Re(geo alpha) + sum_{n = 1}^{N} (||theta^n||^2 - (S_n - theta^n)^2): Pisot's convergence in quantitative form for the cubic complex-pair case; (1) is the case a = 0, b = -1, c = 1, N = 10 (the smallest N with rho^(-N/2) < 1/4; the n = 10 correction term is zero), with Re(geo alpha) = 2 rho^2 + 3 rho - 2 and correction 2 - 2 rho - 2 rho^2. (6) x^3 = x + 1 has exactly one real solution. Statements 4-5 assume neither theta > 1 nor irreducibility. Pisot's theorem itself is not formalized. Not compared, proved in the repository's library only: the threshold from which the Perrin numbers are the nearest integers to rho^n (n >= 10, sharp at n = 9), a claim previously stated without proof at OEIS A001608 (R. Stephan, 2002); it was a compared statement in the withdrawn submissions of 2026-11-03/04 and was removed from the compared set on 2026-11-05 so that every compared result is one first presented here. Application to time (no compared statement asserts it): in the arithmetic of time the tick is multiplication by rho on Q(rho) and the record is the integer lattice; statement 1 says the total squared distance by which the tick history falls short of its record is exactly one tick's unit, rho, and statement 3 says that unit is returned by the two conjugates that are not seen; the quartic companion Q, Q^4 = Q + 1, is not Pisot, so by Pisot's theorem its series diverges (not proved here). That physical time is this arithmetic is the identification stated in the companion entry PALOMAR-2026-08-19-000006 (the arithmetic of time), as an identification; the theorems here are its arithmetic content. That entry's README Scope section is reproduced verbatim in this entry's README.
title: The settling sum of the plastic number: sum_{n >= 1} ||rho^n||^2 = rho. The squared distances from the powers of the plastic number to the nearest integers sum to the plastic number itself; the even-power trace of its two hidden conjugates is rho; with the general cubic complex-pair form

abstract: Kernel-checked proofs, in Lean 4 + Mathlib, of ten statements. Let K be a number field of degree 9 containing a totally real cubic field L and a cubic field M with one real place. Then K = LM has signature (3, 3), and its nine embeddings are the pairs (lambda, mu). A slot assignment, fixed by a labelling of L's embeddings and a non-real embedding mu_1 of M, places the nine conjugates of x in K in a 3 x 3 Hermitian array, the symbol of x; the symbol of x^-1 is its entrywise (Hadamard) inverse. (1) For every finite index type, a positive semidefinite complex matrix with no zero entry has positive semidefinite Hadamard inverse iff it is w w* (rank one); (2) for every complex matrix with no zero entry (positive semidefiniteness not assumed), the Schur multipliers of the matrix and of its Hadamard inverse are both completely positive iff it is w w*. Statements 1-2 are supporting lemmas. (3) The setting: L and M are linearly disjoint, L M = K, and K has 3 real and 3 complex places. (4) The slot assignment exists, is a bijection Fin 3 x Fin 3 ~ (K -> C) with real diagonal and conjugate-symmetric slots, and is unique. (5) For x != 0 in K, the symbol of x is rank one iff N_{K/L}(x) and N_{K/M}(x) are one and the same positive rational number. (6) For a unit u, the symbol is rank one iff N_{K/L}(u) = N_{K/M}(u) = 1. (7) These units H are torsion-free and their logarithmic embedding spans a Z-module of rank 2, so H is isomorphic to Z^2 (the isomorphism is not itself a Lean term). (8) For a unit u, the Schur multipliers of the symbols of u and of u^-1 are both completely positive iff u is in H. (9) There is a unit of infinite order all of whose powers run both ways. (10) The degree-four contrast: in a field with two real places and one complex place, both Schur multipliers of the 2 x 2 place symbol of a unit u and of u^-1 are completely positive iff u is positive at both real places and |sigma(u)| = 1. Statements 4-6, 8 and 9 hold for every labelling and every non-real mu_1. The compositum place bookkeeping is ported, with citation, from the registered entry PALOMAR-2026-10-21-000012; it is not re-proved. Application to time (no compared statement asserts it): in the arithmetic of time the tick is multiplication by a unit; if a unit acts by multiplication on a Hermitian register of its places and an admissible tick must be completely positive, then in degree four a tick u != 1 runs both ways only through a conjugate on the unit circle (Salem type); in a field such as Q(Q), Q^4 = Q + 1, the only such elements are +-1 (not proved in this entry; it follows from statement 17 of the registered entry PALOMAR-2026-10-21-000012, since Q(Q) is contained in Q(rho, Q)), so there the arithmetic gives time a direction; in degree nine a rank-two group of units runs both ways, so the direction is not a property of arithmetic in general: it rests on the degree-four shape and on Q(Q) having no conjugate on the unit circle. The ticks are completely positive, not trace-non-increasing. Companion of the registered entry PALOMAR-2026-08-19-000006 (the arithmetic of time), whose README Scope section is reproduced verbatim in this entry's README.
title: The Arithmetic of Time: reversible units of a degree-nine field. The units of K = LM (L, M cubic) with rank-one Hermitian symbol are exactly those of trivial relative norm to L and to M, a group of rank two, and exactly those whose Schur multipliers run both ways

abstract: A machine-checked proof that an absolutely maximally entangled state of twelve five-level systems exists. The statement and definitions are Formal Conjectures' (Open Quantum Problem 35, `ame_12_5_open`), copied verbatim into Challenge.lean, so this entry proves Formal Conjectures' own statement; one proof step inside the definition combineFirst is changed so that Comparator can match it, and the definition is unchanged. The witness is the graph state of the AME(12, 5) graph of S. Bevins and Y. Bidav. The proof is a general graph-state criterion over ZMod 5 plus 924 kernel-checked cut certificates.
title: An absolutely maximally entangled state of twelve five-level systems: AME(12, 5) exists

abstract: A kernel-checked chirality package for the Padovan substitution (0 ↦ 1, 1 ↦ 2, 2 ↦ 01 on Fin 3; its incidence matrix has characteristic polynomial x³ − x − 1, an orientation fact that is not used or compared). Three compared theorems, all at the iterate-factor level — they quantify over factors of the concrete words S^[n] [x], never over an abstract subshift. (1) The successor invariant: in every positive iterate from any seed, the letter 0 ("a") is immediately followed by 1 ("b"). (2) Chirality: the word 20 ("ca") is a factor of an iterate while its reversal 02 ("ac") is a factor of no iterate from any seed — the factor language reads differently backwards — proved from the invariant, with no enumeration on the ac side. (3) No palindromic factor: no factor of length ≥ 4 of any iterate from any seed (including the zeroth iterate) is a palindrome, via a complete length-≤5 window certificate for the seed a together with the index shift S [0] = [1], S [1] = [2], which exhibits every seed's iterate as a seed-a iterate. These are the three compared statements of the registered record (PALOMAR-2026-08-19-000006 at revision c48eb12), unchanged in this revision. The uniqueness results proved in this repository (Supplement.lean: padovan_minimal_unique, padovan_eigenvalue_unique, padovan_matrix_unique, pisot_ge_plastic, padovan_rules_chiral) are registered separately as PALOMAR-2026-10-18-000019 (stalex444/arithmetic-of-time-slowest-clock, revision 49eafbab4af8899b2a66469697bf74683a88ce87), which compares them over s, mir, inc and sub. Everything else in this repository is public and kernel-checked but not compared: among it the exact orientation threshold (padovan_exact_orientation_threshold_four), the irrationality of the distinguished slope (Time.beta_irrational), mirror identities for arbitrary substitutions, a rate identity, and the characteristic polynomial and chirality of a twelve-letter substitution for ρQ.
title: The Arithmetic of Time: chirality of the Padovan substitution

abstract: A universal inventory of six-coloured MacMahon cubes can build a 2 by 2 by 2 model of every target variety, using eight distinct physical copies, without requiring internal face colours to match. We prove that the minimum inventory size is twelve and classify all ten labelled inventories attaining it, even when repetitions are allowed. They are exactly the two-triangle sets in Conway's tableau. The proof derives row and column sums of two from usability inequalities, proves symmetry, and eliminates every other degree-two inventory by corner coverage. Finite kernel-checked witnesses establish sufficiency. The formalization also verifies the proper cube rotations, outward faces, and completeness and uniqueness of the thirty geometric representatives.
title: The ten minimum universal sets of MacMahon cubes

abstract: Kernel-checked optimum of Hardy's K-step ladder for two qubits (Hardy 1993; Hardy 1997; Boschi, Branca, De Martini and Hardy 1997), for a real Schmidt state c0|00> + c1|11> and real projective settings, the probabilities written out as squared real amplitudes. For every K: under the ladder constraints P(A_K = 1, B_K = 1) <= q^2 (1 - q^{2K})^2 / ((1 + q^2)(1 + q^{2K+1})^2), q = c1/c0, with equality attained (Cereceda 2002, eqs. (18)-(19)); the probability is below 1/2 (the two-qubit, real-settings case of a bound that follows in every dimension from Cereceda 2016, eq. (9), with Wehner 2006), and for every eps > 0 and every large enough K some state and settings exceed 1/2 - eps (the "(50 - delta)%" of Hardy 1997 and Boschi et al. 1997). For every K >= 1 the maximiser of the closed form on (0, 1) is the unique zero there of Cereceda's polynomial m_K (Cereceda 2002, eq. (20), stated there without proof): the derivative of the closed form, the existence and uniqueness of the zero, the maximum and its uniqueness, and, over all Schmidt states and real settings, the optimum, its attainment at the Schmidt ratio r, and that every optimal configuration has Schmidt ratio r or 1/r (attainment at 1/r follows from the uncompared symmetry). Worked instances: the K = 1 optimum is phi^{-5} = (5 sqrt 5 - 11)/2 (Hardy 1993), attained at a state with 2 c0 c1 = 3 - sqrt 5 and only where 2 c0 c1 = 3 - sqrt 5 (Hardy's condition); the K = 2 optimum is (8 rho^2 + rho - 11)/25 = 0.17455..., rho the plastic number (the real root of x^3 - x - 1), attained at Schmidt weights c0^2 = rho^{-1}, c1^2 = rho^{-5} (c1/c0 = rho^{-2}) and only where {c0^2, c1^2} = {rho^{-1}, rho^{-5}}. The value 0.17455 is in print numerically; the closed form, the maximiser rho^{-2}, the weights and the minimal polynomial 25x^3 + 17x^2 + 2x - 1 of the value were not found in the literature searched (2026-10-28) and are the entry's new content. Also: the K = 2 value is not totally real (its minimal polynomial has a non-real complex root). Optimality over complex settings is not formalised. Thirty compared statements.
title: The two-qubit Hardy ladder: the closed form P_K*(q) and its unique maximiser for every K, Hardy's optimum at K = 1, and the optimum (8 rho^2 + rho - 11)/25 in the cubic field Q(rho) at K = 2

abstract: Kernel-checked proofs, in Lean 4 + Mathlib, of the homogeneous case and, at the roots, of the printed form (relations with value in K), with coefficients in any field K of characteristic 0, of the additive theorem for 2-transitive Galois groups (Girstmair, Manuscripta Math. 39 (1982) 81-97, Proposition 4, Assertion 3, p. 86, for every field whose characteristic does not divide |G|; stated by J. D. Dixon, Acta Arith. 82 (1997) 293-302, as Theorem 1', p. 301, with its proof omitted), of its representation-theoretic engine (classical: Huppert, Endliche Gruppen I, p. 597, Satz 20.2, as cited by Girstmair, Acta Arith. 89 (1999) 53-96, p. 78; used by Dixon on p. 297, in the proof of Theorem 1(ii), citing Curtis-Reiner Section 32B), and of two criterion forms over any field whose hypothesis is the irreducibility of the augmentation module instead of 2-transitivity (the 'if' direction of Girstmair 1982, Proposition 4, Assertion 2, in its module form). Eight compared theorems, in namespace DixonRelations, in this order. (1) zeroSum_irreducible, the engine: for a finite group G acting 2-transitively on a finite set Omega with 2 <= |Omega| and a field K of characteristic 0, the augmentation (zero-sum) subspace V0 = {f : Omega -> K | sum_x f x = 0} of the permutation module Omega -> K is an irreducible K[G]-module; proved in the substantive form of simplicity, that a G-invariant subspace W <= V0 with W != bot equals V0. The G-action is the permutation representation (g . f) x = f (g^{-1} . x), and a subrepresentation is a Submodule together with an explicit invariance hypothesis. (2') additive_core_of_irreducible, the zero-sum criterion form: for any field K, any group G (finite or not) acting on a finite Omega, an injective family alpha : Omega -> L into a K-vector space L, K-linear maps phi g with phi g (alpha x) = alpha (g . x) (no homomorphism property assumed), and the hypothesis hirr (every nonzero G-invariant K-subspace of V0 is V0, word for word the conclusion of (1); it holds vacuously when V0 = 0, that is |Omega| <= 1), any c with sum_x c x = 0 and sum_x c x . alpha x = 0 is 0. (2) additive_core, the zero-sum form for an abstract family: the same conclusion for K of characteristic 0 and a finite group G acting 2-transitively on Omega with 2 <= |Omega|; it is (1) followed by (2'). (3) additive_roots_no_relation, the zero-sum form at the roots: for K of characteristic 0 and an irreducible f in K[X] of degree >= 2 whose Galois group acts 2-transitively on the roots of f in the splitting field, any K-valued coefficient tuple c on the roots with sum_r c r = 0 and sum_r c r . r = 0 is 0; G = f.Gal, Omega = f.rootSet f.SplittingField (with Mathlib's instance Polynomial.Gal.galActionAux), the family is the inclusion of the root set, phi g is the field automorphism g read as a K-linear map (the compatibility holds by rfl), and 2 <= |Omega| follows from card_rootSet_eq_natDegree with separability from Irreducible.separable; f.SplittingField appears in the 2-transitivity hypothesis and in the types of c and of the relation hypothesis. (3) is the zero-sum part (value 0, coefficient sum 0) of the homogeneous case of Dixon's Theorem 1' at the roots; the full homogeneous case at the roots is (5), and the inhomogeneous case is (6). (4') relModule_le_span_one_of_irreducible, the span-one criterion form: under the hypotheses of (2') and a transitive action, every coefficient tuple c with sum_x c x . alpha x = 0 is a scalar multiple of the all-ones tuple, i.e. relModule K alpha is contained in the line K . (fun _ => 1). This is the 'if' direction of Girstmair 1982, Proposition 4, Assertion 2 (p. 86: "If G is primitive on G/H, (G,H) admits only trivial relations over K iff the complementary module U(G/H) of K epsilon_0 is simple"), whose hypothesis is, like hirr, the simplicity of a module; Girstmair 1999 restates it in character form as Proposition 12 (p. 78), "essentially contained in Proposition 4 of [11]". (4') assumes transitivity in place of primitivity; for a transitive action, hirr already forces primitivity (elementary, not formalized: the zero-sum functions constant on the blocks of a nontrivial block system form a nonzero proper invariant subspace of V0), so the difference is one of form only. (4) relModule_le_span_one, the span-one form: the same conclusion under the hypotheses of (2); it is (1) followed by (4'). (5) relModule_roots_le_span_one, the span-one form at the roots: under the hypotheses of (3), relModule K of the root family (fun r => (r : f.SplittingField)) is contained in K . (fun _ => 1); it is (4) at the roots. (6) roots_inhomogeneous_iff_const, Dixon's printed form at the roots: under the hypotheses of (3), sum_r c r . r = algebraMap K f.SplittingField k for some k in K if and only if c is constant; in Dixon's notation this is U = K.e. Dixon's Theorem 1' is stated for any subfield K of C and for relations with value in K; compared statements (2), (3), (4) and (5) concern its homogeneous case (value 0) and (6) its printed form (value in K), for every field K of characteristic 0, and (2') and (4') take any field. Girstmair 1982 states the additive theorem for every field whose characteristic does not divide |G|, so characteristic 0 is a sub-case of his hypothesis; (2') and (4') take any field, but their content is carried by hirr, which this entry proves only in characteristic 0 and only for 2-transitive actions, as (1). An uncompared bridge, BDS.isAtom_zeroSumSubrep_iff, shows that hirr together with V0 != bot is atomicity of V0 in Mathlib's lattice of subrepresentations of the permutation representation on Omega -> K. (1) is proved by an elementary, character-free stabilizer-averaging argument; Dixon (p. 297) cites Curtis-Reiner Section 32B for the statement only; Curtis-Reiner was not consulted, and nothing is claimed about its proof. (2') applies hirr to relModule K alpha meet V0 and uses injectivity of alpha; (4') shows that a relation and each of its translates differ by a zero-sum relation, so the relation is G-invariant, hence constant by transitivity (no averaging); the forward direction of (6) argues in the same way at the roots for a relation with value in K, using (2), and its reverse direction uses that the sum of the roots of a separable polynomial is fixed by every automorphism of the splitting field, which is Galois over K, and so lies in K. This formalizes classical results; it is not new mathematics. Research context: additive and multiplicative relations among conjugate algebraic numbers are studied in Girstmair (1982, 1999), Smyth (1986), Drmota-Skalba (1991), Baron-Drmota-Skalba (1995), Dixon (1997) and Zheng (2021); in the sources read for this entry the doubly transitive additive case is derived from the criterion and character theory in one sentence (Girstmair 1982, p. 86), set aside because the doubly transitive pairs are classified (Girstmair 1999, p. 78), and stated with its proof omitted (Dixon 1997, p. 301); this entry gives a complete, character-free, machine-checked proof. The namespace BDS of the two entry definitions is the development's historical name (after Baron-Drmota-Skalba); no result of Baron-Drmota-Skalba is formalized. Formalization status (search of 2026-10-28 for the six statements (1), (2'), (2), (3), (4') and (4) as stated here, at the repository heads listed in README.md; a search result, not a guarantee): none of the six statements searched was found in any prover; (5) and (6), searched for on 2026-10-29 at the repository heads listed in README.md, were not found either. The fact behind the reverse direction of (6), that the sum of the roots lies in the base field, is in Mathlib at the pin in Vieta form (Polynomial.Splits.nextCoeff_eq_neg_sum_roots_mul_leadingCoeff), for the multiset of roots. The S_n case of (1) is formalized in augmentation form over every field in which |Omega| != 0 (every field when |Omega| = 2), in particular over Q, in TauCeti (TauCeti.isIrreducible_standardRepresentation, since 2026-08-05) and as Specht-module irreducibility over C in openai/math; the general 2-transitive case of (1) is formalized in character form over C in AxiomMath/CFSG (CFSG.permutation_character_orbit_count, public since 2026-10-27), the closest item found: CFSG also defines the same V0 over C under the same action (CFSG.Wreathed.CentralSL2.sumZeroSubrep) and computes its character, from which the C case of (1) in submodule form would follow in a few lines, but no theorem stating it was found. NOT formalized and NOT claimed: the MULTIPLICATIVE theorem (Dixon Theorem 1(ii), and, per Zheng 2021, arXiv:1912.07202v1, p. 2, Baron-Drmota-Skalba 1995, Theorem 3), under which 2-transitivity does NOT force triviality: for a prime p and b in Q not a p-th power, X^p - b has Galois group AGL(1,p) over Q, acting sharply 2-transitively on the roots, and the ratios of its roots are p-th roots of unity, nontrivial multiplicative relations; Dixon's Theorem 1(ii) gives necessary conditions for that exception; none of that multiplicative content is proved or claimed here. The additive theorem carries no such exception, because the additive module cannot contain any e_gamma - e_delta (Dixon, p. 301). Also not formalized: the 2-transitivity of any particular Galois group (a hypothesis in (1), (2), (3), (4), (5) and (6)); any case of hirr other than the 2-transitive one, (1); the imprimitive case (Girstmair 1982, Proposition 4, Assertion 1; Girstmair 1999, Proposition 12, first sentence) and the fact that hirr forces primitivity for a transitive action; the 'only if' direction of the criterion, the character form of its hypothesis, and the converse of Assertion 3 that Girstmair 1982 states for a splitting field; and the identification of Omega -> K with the scalar extension of Omega -> Q.
title: The additive theorem for 2-transitive Galois groups (Girstmair; Dixon, Theorem 1') and its representation-theoretic engine

abstract: This entry states correctness results, in exact rational arithmetic, for an executable implementation of the two-locus sampling recursion of the coalescent with recombination under parent-independent mutation, with two alleles at each locus. For valid parameters and configurations with the stated array sizes, the computation succeeds and its value equals the solution of the recursion at the decoded configuration. A table checker is shown to be sound and complete: a table that passes the check consists of true values of the recursion, and the table of true values over the closure of configurations of a given size passes. The existence of a solution to the recursion, for any finite numbers of alleles, positive mutation rates, and nonnegative recombination rate, is also stated, together with an explicit characterization of the Boolean parameter-validity test.
title: A kernel-checked implementation of the biallelic two-locus sampling recursion, and a table checker

abstract: Kernel-checked transfer of the exact CHSH constants for self-adjoint involutions (Mathlib's IsCHSHTuple in a C*-normed ring: the norm of the CHSH operator T = A0 B0 + A0 B1 + A1 B0 - A1 B1 is at most 2*sqrt(2), equals 2 under a commuting party (the equality in a nontrivial real C*-normed algebra; the <= forms in every C*-normed ring), and exceeds 2 only if both parties are noncommuting) to self-adjoint CONTRACTIONS, together with the state corollary. A CHSH contraction tuple is four self-adjoint operators of norm at most 1 with the four cross-party commutations - IsCHSHTuple with the involution relations relaxed to norm bounds. The route is the Halmos dilation A -> A (x) Z + sqrt(1 - A^2) (x) X (Halmos 1950), applied with ONE ANCILLA PER OBSERVABLE: the four dilations form a Mathlib IsCHSHTuple on n (x) (C^2)^(x)4, every commutation relation among the four observables transfers to the dilations, the dilated CHSH operator compresses to T, and compression does not increase the operator norm, so every involution bound transfers. One ancilla per party would not do: for B0 = 1, B1 = 0 the single-ancilla dilations 1 (x) Z and 1 (x) X anticommute, so the commuting-party bound would not transfer. Nine compared statements: for n x n complex matrices (l2-operator norm), norm T <= 2*sqrt(2), norm T <= 2 if either party commutes, and 2 < norm T forces both parties noncommuting; for every density matrix rho, (1/2)|Re tr(rho T)| <= sqrt(2), and <= 1 under a commuting party; the same three norm bounds for bounded operators on a complete complex inner-product space (ampliation on the Hilbert sum WithLp 2 (E x E)); and, RESTATED, the parallelogram bound norm(A0 (B0 + B1) + A1 (B0 - B1)) <= 2*sqrt(2) for four operators of norm at most 1 with no self-adjointness and no commutation (folklore; formalized in Lean by Physical Superintelligence, 2026-10-23; proved independently here). The involution constants are the author's registered entry PALOMAR-2026-08-19-000007, re-proved here as library support and not compared. The bounds themselves are classical (Tsirelson 1980; the commuting-algebra bound as used by Summers and Werner 1987); new in this entry, relative to the Lean prior art recorded under sources (PSI's parallelogram and Hilbert-space state bounds; Lean-QIT's Kronecker-form state bound for contractions), are the contraction statements in the forms stated and their derivation from the involution constants by dilation (statements 1 and 6 are, as statements, the self-adjoint cross-commuting case of the parallelogram bound; their novelty is the route). The Challenge imports Mathlib only; the three structures it uses (IsCHSHContractionTuple for matrices, IsDensityMatrix, Hilbert.IsCHSHContractionTuple for operators) are verbatim copies of the library's, checked byte for byte by scripts/check_challenge_definitions.py. The Mathlib definitions the statements import (the scoped l2-operator norm on matrices, PosSemidef under ComplexOrder, IsSelfAdjoint and the adjoint, the trace, the operator norm, WithLp 2, IsCHSHTuple) are quoted verbatim from the pinned source with permalinks in MATHLIB_DEFINITIONS.md and kernel-checked in DefinitionAudit.lean, a default build target that is not compared.
title: CHSH bounds for contractions by dilation: Tsirelson's bound, the classical bound under a commuting party, and the necessity of noncommutativity

abstract: A Lean 4 and Mathlib formalization of Conjecture 7.3 of arXiv:2609.35632 on the central configurations of the planar Newtonian four-body problem. At every strictly convex central configuration of four positive masses, the Hessian form Q of U + (λ/2)I is at least two thirds of its radial part K, and strictly so wherever K is positive. In the notation of the paper this is λ_max(G) < 1/3 for the explicit 2×2 matrix G of its Proposition 3.5, and by its Proposition 7.2 the constant 2/3 is optimal. It sharpens Theorem B of the paper, Q ≥ K/4. The definitions and the reduction to the normal form of Corbera, Cors and Roberts are those of the registered development lean4body-uniqueness. The new parts are a majorant that pays only the largest eigenvalue of S(y), an exact test that is positive definite exactly when λ_max(G) < 1/3, and a computer-assisted proof of that test: a branch and bound with interval arithmetic over the three-dimensional set of normalized convex central configurations, reduced by a symmetry to half of it, and an exact Taylor-form theorem at the corner where the margin of the test vanishes. Lean's kernel checks the certificates with `decide +kernel`. The trusted base is Lean's kernel, including its built-in arithmetic on natural-number literals (GMP-accelerated), and the proofs use only Lean's three standard axioms.
title: The optimal Hessian bound for convex four-body central configurations

abstract: A complete Lean 4 / Mathlib formalization of R. M. Wilson's "Nonisomorphic Steiner triple systems" (inequality (2.1), Theorems 1–4, Lemmas 3–5, including the exact numbers of Latin squares of orders 6, 7 and 8 and the bounds N(19) ≥ 2450, N(21) ≥ 2160980, N(25) ≥ 163929929318400) and of N. Linial and Z. Luria's "An upper bound on the number of Steiner triple systems" (Theorems 1.1 and 1.2 with explicit error terms). Version 2 adds a proof of the van der Waerden permanent theorem (Egorychev, Falikman), following Gurvits's proof as simplified by Laurent and Schrijver. The parts of Wilson's Theorems 2 and 3 that rely on it are stated both as implications from the hypothesis vdWPC, as in the paper, and unconditionally (theorem2_full, theorem3_full). Finite computations are kernel-checked certificates (no native_decide). Mathlib does not contain these results.
title: Counting Steiner triple systems: Wilson (1974) and Linial–Luria (2013)

abstract:
Kernel-checked proofs, in Lean 4 + Mathlib, about cut-and-project schemes on a fixed integer lattice Z^iota invariant under an integer matrix A: splittings R^iota = E + H into A-invariant subspaces with Z^iota meeting H only in 0 and the projection of Z^iota to H dense in H, a window W in H (bounded, containing a relative ball), the model set Lambda(W) = {pi_E g : g in Z^iota, pi_H g in W}, and admissibility, some window with A Lambda(W) contained in Lambda(W) (inflation symmetry in Meyer's inclusion sense). The least physical dimension d(A) is the least dim E over admissible schemes. Thirteen compared theorems. (1) For every integer A, a scheme is admissible iff A is power-bounded on H; then the orbit window is a compact convex symmetric invariant window; the per-window criterion; and U(A) <= dim E, U(A) the number of eigenvalues of modulus > 1. (2) Kronecker's density criterion in cut-and-project form. (3) For every integer A with det A != 0, any chi_A: (a) d(A) is the sum over the distinct irreducible factors p of chi_A over Q of m_p u_p + c_p (m_p - r_1(p)), plus min(deg p, 2) when every root of p lies on the unit circle and r_1(p) = m_p, where m_p is the multiplicity, u_p and c_p count the roots of p of modulus > 1 and = 1, and r_1(p) = (2 dim ker p(A) - dim ker p(A)^2) / deg p (ranks over Q) is the number of Jordan blocks of size one at each root of p; (b) the value is an invariant of rational similarity; (c) the factors with all roots on the unit circle are the cyclotomic ones; and (d) for chi_A squarefree every invariant splitting is E = ker q_E(A), H = ker q_H(A) with chi_A = q_E q_H, it is admissible iff the roots of q_H lie in the closed unit disk and every irreducible rational factor of chi_A shares a root with q_E, and d(A) = U(A) + circleCount(A), counting 1 for each factor x - 1, x + 1 and 2 for each other cyclotomic factor, each with its multiplicity. (4) For det A != 0 and hyperbolic A, any chi_A and no diagonalizability: a scheme is admissible iff E contains the unstable set iff H lies in the stable set; an invariant splitting carries an admissible scheme iff E contains the unstable set; d(A) = U(A), attained only by the unstable/stable splitting. (5) For det A != 0, any chi_A: d(A) = 1 iff chi_A is irreducible with exactly one root of modulus > 1 (a real root, a Pisot or Salem number up to sign, or an integer on Z^1), or A = +-1 in any rank; in the irreducible case every admissible line is the eigenline. (6) If A^k = 1: every factor is cyclotomic and d = sum of min(deg p, 2) over the distinct factors; the same for chi_A squarefree with all roots on the unit circle; every integer matrix with chi_A = Phi_n, n >= 3 (multiplication by a primitive n-th root of unity), needs exactly a plane. (7) Jordan blocks on the circle: I_2 and the Jordan block J_2 both have chi = (x - 1)^2, for which the squarefree count of (3), with x - 1 counted twice, gives 2, but d = 1 and 2; 1 + J_2(1) and 1 + J_3(1) have d = 2 and 3. (8) Multiplication by rho, rho^-1, Q and theta = -Q^-1 = 1 - Q^3 on Z[rho] and Z[Q] (rho^3 = rho + 1, Q^4 = Q + 1): d = 1, 2, 3, 1. (9) On Z[rho] (x) Z[Q] (degree 12), multiplication by every alpha other than 0, +-1 is nonsingular (det != 0) and hyperbolic with d = U; for rho, theta, rho Q and Q the values are 4, 3, 5, 9. (10) rho and theta act on their unstable spaces as real scalars, and the spectral projection carries the quartic (resp. cubic) sector onto them with the Gram pairing GramRho (x) GramQ equal to that of GramQ (resp. GramRho), of types (3,1) and (2,1). (11) The scheme of Q on Z^4 with an interval window: a segment, an explicit Q-invariant model set in R^3, determinant -1/q' on E, non-real moduli, and the types (2,1) and (1,0) of the trace form on E and H. (12) A Salem witness, the companion of x^4 - x^3 - x^2 - x + 1: not hyperbolic, d = 1. (13) Every model set is a Delone set (Mathlib's Delone.DeloneSet) with uniformly discrete difference set. The mathematics of (1), (2), (4), (5) for irreducible chi_A, and (13), and of (6) for chi_A = Phi_n, is known in other formulations (Masakova-Mazac-Pelantova 2021; Kronecker, Pleasants 2000; Harriss-Koivusalo-Walton 2025, preprint; Meyer 1972, 1995; Lagarias 1999; Solomyak 2020; the classical cyclotomic model sets; Moody 1997); (1) and (4) are stated with no diagonalizability hypothesis. The scheme and model set of (11) are, in substance, instances of Masakova-Mazac-Pelantova Thm 13.1 and of Harriss-Koivusalo-Walton Section 3.4, and are not new. For squarefree chi_A the count of (3) also follows from the arguments of Masakova-Mazac-Pelantova (Lemma 5.1, Prop. 8.1(iii), Cor. 13.4), stated there for generic (aperiodic) schemes; the lattice-first least physical dimension was not found stated in the sources read (search completed 2026-10-20). Beyond the cited cases, the entry proves the least physical dimension for every nonsingular integer matrix (3), including what lies outside the diagonalizable class of Masakova-Mazac-Pelantova: a Jordan block of size >= 2 at an eigenvalue on the unit circle counts in full (the terms c_p (m_p - r_1(p)), which vanish for diagonalizable A), and at a cyclotomic factor with such a block the blocks of size one cost nothing, the internal space being tilted into the socle of the larger blocks; the witnesses are J_2, 1 + J_2(1) and 1 + J_3(1) (7). Every admissible scheme of an A with such a block at a root of unity has Z^iota meeting E in a nonzero vector. It also proves the characterization of every admissible splitting for squarefree chi_A ((3)(d)), non-generic splittings included (its necessity half is the injectivity argument of Masakova-Mazac-Pelantova, Lemma 5.1), and (1) for every integer matrix and (4) for every nonsingular hyperbolic integer matrix, with no diagonalizability hypothesis; for diagonalizable A and generic schemes, the uniqueness of the minimal scheme in (4) and of the minimal physical line in (5) is immediate from Masakova-Mazac-Pelantova, Cor. 13.4. For det A != 0 and squarefree chi_A with a factor Phi_n, n not in {1, 2, 3, 4, 6}, the minimal scheme is not unique, by (3)(d). The companion matrices are multiplication by rho and Q in the power bases by definition, so Crho^i (x) CQ^j is multiplication by rho^i Q^j in the product basis. That the rho^i Q^j are a Z-basis of the ring of integers of Q(rho, Q) is statement (8) of the author's registered entry PALOMAR-2026-10-21-000012 (stalex444/pdt-hermite-signature-compositum@5aa870e98236ba240561b798265c629df8c2d031); that GramRho, GramQ and GramRho (x) GramQ are the Gram matrices of the trace forms in these bases is statements (8), (9) and (19) of the author's registered entry PALOMAR-2026-09-02-000014, in which Q(rho) (x) Q(Q) is the field Q(rho, Q) (its (23)). These are cited, not compared. Application (cited, not a claim of the entry): In the author's Pisot Dimensional Theory, Q(rho) is the arithmetic of three-dimensional space and Q(Q) the arithmetic of four-dimensional spacetime, and their compositum K, whose integers are Z[rho] (x) Z[Q], is the parent of both (the author's registered entry PALOMAR-2026-10-21-000012 (stalex444/pdt-hermite-signature-compositum@5aa870e98236ba240561b798265c629df8c2d031), statements (7), (8)). A model set is the shadow of a lattice cut through a window, a standard mathematical model of a quasicrystal (Moody 2000). Read through the theory, this entry's theorems fix how many dimensions each of the theory's inflations needs to be the symmetry of one, and which ones.
Space inflates the parent through spacetime, and spacetime inflates it through space. On the parent's lattice the plastic inflation rho needs exactly four physical dimensions, and only one scheme attains four (4, 9). Those four are a copy of spacetime's: rho has a single expanding embedding in Q(rho), the real one, and the spectral projection maps the quartic sector onto them, carrying Z[Q] with its trace form unchanged, of Lorentzian type (3,1) (10). rho acts on them as a pure dilation by rho = 1.3247..., the same stretch in every direction (10). (8, 9, 10). Taken over all three embeddings of Q(rho) instead of the one expanding embedding, the form on the quartic sector is tripled: the factor 3 of statement (13) of PALOMAR-2026-10-21-000012.
The clock needs one dimension; the ruler needs five. On Z[rho] the plastic inflation needs exactly one: the line, over a two-dimensional window at the complex place (8). The plastic substitution's control-point sets are regular model sets in this scheme, with Rauzy-fractal windows in C (Baake and Grimm 2020), and in the theory the line is time and its points are the ticks (PALOMAR-2026-08-19-000006, PALOMAR-2026-10-18-000019). Off the parent, eigenvalues on the unit circle can change the count: a Salem inflation's circle eigendirections lie in the internal space and cost nothing, so it still needs only a line (5, 12), but multiplication by a primitive n-th root of unity, n >= 3, needs exactly a plane, and every element of finite order n >= 3 needs at least one (6). The parent has none. No element of K other than +-1 has a conjugate on the unit circle (statement (17) of PALOMAR-2026-10-21-000012), so every inflation of the parent by an element other than 0 and +-1 is hyperbolic, needs exactly as many dimensions as it has expanding embeddings (a complex place counts twice), and has a unique minimal scheme (4, 9).

abstract: A complete Lean 4 / Mathlib formalization of Theorems 1, 2 and 3 of Duminil-Copin, Sidoravicius and Tassion (arXiv:1505.04159v1). Theorem 3: for the random-cluster model on the square lattice with any real cluster weight q >= 1, at its critical point p_c, the following are equivalent: the origin lies in an infinite cluster with probability 0 under the wired measure; equality of the free and wired measures; infinite susceptibility of the free measure; sub-exponential decay of the free one-arm probability; and the RSW bound for free boundary conditions at distance n. title: Continuity of the phase transition for planar random-cluster and Potts models with 1 <= q <= 4 (Theorems 1, 2 and 3)

abstract: A Lean 4 proof of the characterization of Hamiltonian paths in rectangular grid graphs by Itai, Papadimitriou and Szwarcfiter (1982, Theorem 3.2). For distinct vertices s and t of the width × height grid graph, a Hamiltonian path from s to t exists if and only if the problem is acceptable, that is, colour compatible (by the checkerboard colouring) and not one of the three forbidden configurations F1, F2, F3 on grids of width or height 1, 2 or 3. Necessity is proved for each forbidden case, where the paper only says "a straightforward case analysis". Sufficiency is proved by strong induction with an explicit reduction rule (strip two columns or split at a cut edge) and 596 kernel-checked base-case paths.
title: Hamiltonian paths in rectangular grid graphs (Itai, Papadimitriou and Szwarcfiter)

abstract: Lean formalization of five manuscript result groups: Theorems 1.1, 1.3, and 1.6, and Corollaries 1.2 and 1.7. abstract:
Kernel-checked proofs, in Lean 4 + Mathlib, of six general theorems and twelve statements about one number field. General: (1) Hermite's signature theorem for every real polynomial f, degenerate case included and with no monic hypothesis: the power-sum Hankel (Hermite) form H_f has sigPos = #R + #C+, sigNeg = #C+, rank sigPos + sigNeg = #D and radical of dimension deg f - #D, where D, R, C+ are the distinct complex roots, the real ones, and those in the upper half plane; (2) its number-field form (classical, Hermite-Sylvester; in number-field form credited to O. Taussky 1968): the trace form Tr_{K/Q}(x^2) of a number field K has type (r1 + r2, r2), and is positive definite iff K is totally real; (3) the places of a linearly disjoint compositum L = K1 K2: r1(L) = r1(K1) r1(K2) and 2 r2(L) = [K1:Q][K2:Q] - r1(K1) r1(K2); (4) the signed discriminant of such a compositum with coprime discriminants, d_L = d_{K1}^[K2:Q] d_{K2}^[K1:Q], the sign included; (5) the trace projection [E:F]^-1 Tr_{E/F} onto a subfield F, the orthogonal decomposition E = F + F^perp for Tr_{E/Q}(xy) with F^perp = ker Tr_{E/F}, the restriction of the trace form of E to F as [E:F] times the trace form of F, and the type (r1(E) + r2(E) - r1(F) - r2(F), r2(E) - r2(F)) of its restriction to ker Tr_{E/F}; (6) the squarefree-discriminant criterion (a textbook exercise). The field: the compositum L of Q(rho) and Q(Q), rho and Q roots of x^3 - x - 1 and x^4 - x - 1, built as the tower K3 = Q[X]/(X^3 - X - 1), L = K3[Y]/(Y^4 - Y - 1), of degree 12: (7) the setting (degrees 3, 4, 12; linearly disjoint sectors); (8) O_{Q(rho)} = Z[rho], O_{Q(Q)} = Z[Q], discriminants -23 and -283, O_L = Z[rho, Q] with basis rho^i Q^j; (9) d_L = (-23)^4 (-283)^3 = -6342648595267; (10) places (1,1), (2,1), (2,5) and the trace-form type (7,5) of L, derived from (2) and (3) with no root located; (11) the relative traces on the product basis; (12) Tr(-alpha^-1) = 1 for alpha^n = alpha + 1 in degree n, the unit sections -Q^-1 and -rho^-1 of the relative traces, their surjectivity on rings of integers and the integral splittings of ranks 3 + 9 and 4 + 8; (13) the orthogonal decompositions of L along the two sectors, with restrictions 4 Tr and 3 Tr of types (2,1), (3,1) and complements of types (5,4), (4,4); (14) the covolume 2^-5 23^2 283 sqrt(283) of O_L in Mathlib's normalization, which is 4 times the product covol(O_{Q(rho)})^4 covol(O_{Q(Q)})^3; (15) the discriminant -23^4 53^2 283^3 of the degree-12 polynomial, which is the minimal polynomial of rho Q, and the index [O_L : Z[rho Q]] = 53; (16) the subfield lattice {Q, Q(rho), Q(Q), L}; (17) root-rigidity and circle-freeness of L; (18) Smyth's lower bound for the Mahler measure on O_L, with Smyth's theorem as an explicit hypothesis (cited, not proved). Eighteen compared theorems. The mathematics of (1)-(6) is classical and no novelty is claimed for it; the contribution is the kernel-checked proofs: (1), (2) and (5) from Mathlib's sigPos, sigNeg (D. Loeffler) and, for (2) and (5), Algebra.traceForm, between which Mathlib has no theorem at the pinned revision; (3) and (4) from Mathlib's infinite places and linear disjointness. The proof modules also prove, not compared, that sigPos and sigNeg are additive over orthogonal direct sums and invariant under positive scaling over any linearly ordered field, and that the signature of a rational matrix form is unchanged by base change to R; Mathlib at the pin has none of these. Mathlib prior art is used and not re-proved: X. Roblot's theorem on the absolute value of the discriminant of a coprime compositum (statement (4) adds the sign) and his theorem on its ring of integers (used in (8)). The definiteness corollary of (1) (real-rooted iff H_f positive semidefinite) was formalized in Lean 4 by P. Alexandersson (RealRooted, 2026-09-27) before this entry; (1) proves the full rank/signature/radical count, from which that corollary follows. No prior formalization of the rank and signature count of the Hermite form, or of the trace-form signature (r1 + r2, r2) of a number field, was found by a search on 2026-10-19 (Mathlib, the Isabelle AFP, Coq/MathComp, HOL Light, Lean 4 community repositories, Zenodo, arXiv); the existing root-counting formalizations use sign variations of remainder sequences. The sector inputs of the field at the level of Q are ported from the author's registered entry PALOMAR-2026-09-02-000014 and are not compared; (7) and the minimal-polynomial clause of (15) re-prove facts certified in the author's registered entry PALOMAR-2026-09-01-000005 and are not new. Application (cited, not a claim of the entry): In the author's Pisot Dimensional Theory, Q(rho) is the arithmetic of three-dimensional space and Q(Q) the arithmetic of four-dimensional spacetime, and their compositum K is the parent of both. Read through the theory, this entry's theorems make six conclusions exact.
Space and spacetime are the only worlds the parent contains. The fields between Q and K have degrees 3 and 4 and no others: Q(rho) and Q(Q) are K's only proper subfields other than Q (16). An intermediate sub-arithmetic of the parent has dimension 3 or 4, and nothing else; there is no 2-, 6- or other intermediate world.
The world is a product, not a sum. K is the tensor product of the two sectors, 12 = 3*4 (7), and its integers are exactly Z[rho] (x) Z[Q] (8). The parent's discrete structure is built from the two sectors' lattices and nothing else.
The parent's geometry is the product of space's and spacetime's. The trace form of K has type (7,5) (10), and it is the tensor product of the sectors' own forms (PALOMAR-2026-09-02-000014): (2,1) (x) (3,1), with 2*3 + 1*1 = 7 and 2*1 + 1*3 = 5. On the quartic sector the form is 3 times spacetime's own, of Lorentzian type (3,1); on the cubic sector, 4 times space's, of type (2,1) (13). The one time direction is not put in by hand: it is what the parent's form is on spacetime.
All of the parent's asymmetry between space and time is spacetime's. The parent's excess of positive over negative directions, 7 - 5 = 2, is exactly spacetime's 3 - 1 = 2. The eight dimensions orthogonal to spacetime are perfectly balanced, four positive and four negative (5, 13).
Both sectors are recovered from the parent. The relative traces, divided by the relative degrees [K:Q(rho)] = 4 and [K:Q(Q)] = 3, are the orthogonal projections onto the sectors (5), and the traces themselves carry the parent's lattice onto Z[rho] and Z[Q] (12). Every element of space and of spacetime is the shadow of an element of the parent.
The parent is built from minimizers, and joining them creates nothing smaller. Each sector's generator is a minimizer, certified in the author's registered entries: x^3 - x - 1 and x^4 - x - 1 attain the least Mahler measure above 1 among irreducible integer polynomials of degrees 3 and 4 (PALOMAR-2026-08-31-000004); rho is the least Pisot eigenvalue of any substitution on at most three letters, the slowest settling clock (PALOMAR-2026-10-18-000019), and the growth rate of the triangle group (2,3,infinity) = PGL(2,Z), the slowest of the hyperbolic triangle groups (p,q,infinity) (PALOMAR-2026-10-17-000013). K is the compositum of the two minimizers, and a single number generates all of it: rho*Q, the theory's coupling ruler (15; PALOMAR-2026-09-01-000005). Minimality survives the join. No element of K other than +/-1 has a conjugate on the unit circle (17), so the parent contains no Salem number, and with Smyth's theorem every nonzero integer of K other than +/-1 has Mahler measure at least rho (18), with equality at rho itself (PALOMAR-2026-08-31-000004). The 3D generator is the smallest nontrivial size in the whole twelve-dimensional arithmetic, exactly as in degree 3. In the theory, rho is the ground of minimality and therefore the ground of three-dimensional structure; joining space to spacetime keeps that ground.
The two sectors are the two sides of the Pisot boundary. rho is a Pisot number, and the Padovan substitution tiling, whose characteristic polynomial is x^3 - x - 1, is a regular model set with pure-point diffraction (Baake and Grimm 2020): the ordered, classical sector. It is handed, the arrow of time: its tiling flow is neither mutually locally derivable from nor topologically conjugate to its mirror image (Gaehler 2026, Example 10 and Remark 7, where the Padovan rule is varrho_R after renaming a <-> c), and in the factor language the author's registered entries PALOMAR-2026-08-19-000006, PALOMAR-2026-09-04-000004 and PALOMAR-2026-10-18-000019 certify it: ca occurs and ac never does. Q is not Pisot (PALOMAR-2026-09-01-000012), and every primitive self-similar tiling of the line with expansion Q has no non-trivial pure-point spectrum (Solomyak 1997): the quantum sector, which cannot settle on a line. This is the arithmetic of a quasicrystal (superspace crystallography: de Wolff 1974; Janner and Janssen 1977; cut-and-project: de Bruijn 1981; Kramer and Neri 1984; Duneau and Katz 1985; Elser 1986): a higher-dimensional lattice, O_K in R^2 x C^5, from which the sector lattices are recovered by the traces (12).
title: Hermite's signature theorem and the coprime compositum, with the degree-12 compositum of x^3 - x - 1 and x^4 - x - 1

abstract: A complete Lean 4 / Mathlib formalization of Theorems 1.1 and 1.2 of Duminil-Copin, Gagnebin, Harel, Manolescu and Tassion (arXiv:1611.09877v2). For the q-state Potts model on the square lattice with q > 4, at beta_c = log(1 + sqrt q), the q + 1 box-limit Gibbs measures are distinct and ergodic, each monochromatic measure gives its own colour probability greater than 1/q at the origin, and the inverse correlation length in the diagonal direction is lambda + 2 sum_{k >= 1} (-1)^k tanh(k lambda) / k, where cosh lambda = sqrt(q) / 2, a positive number.
