abstract: Kernel-checked classification of the morphic numbers — the reals p > 1 satisfying both of the golden ratio's defining scale closures: p + 1 = p^k (the sum of consecutive measures of the geometric system is again a measure) and p - 1 = p^(-l) (so is their difference; rendered zpow-free as p^l * (p - 1) = 1). These two equations are the arithmetic of self-similar proportion: a number satisfying both generates a measure system closed under the paper's superposition and juxtaposition, the property pair behind the divine proportion's standing as the plane's design constant. The theorem (Aarts-Fokkink-Kruijtzer 2001): there exist only two such numbers — the golden ratio, with (k, l) = (2, 1), and the plastic number, the real root of x^3 = x + 1, with (k, l) = (3, 4). Four compared statements carry the classification in full: existence of the cubic's root, the iff pinning every morphic number to the golden ratio or that root, and the two witnesses. The list of numbers with the golden ratio's defining property pair is thereby provably complete at two. The second member is a distinguished constant independently of this theorem: the plastic number is the smallest Pisot number (Siegel 1944); its minimal polynomial x^3 - x - 1 attains the minimal Mahler measure among monic irreducible integer cubics (kernel-certified in the registered entry PALOMAR-2026-08-31-000004), and by Smyth's theorem its measure — the number itself — is the global minimum of the Mahler measure over nonreciprocal integer polynomials; it is the growth rate of the Padovan and Perrin sequences, the cubic analogue of Fibonacci growth; and it is the threshold constant of the Blanc-Cantat classification of birational surface dynamical degrees, the spectral limit of the Bedford-Kim automorphism family (kernel-certified in the author's mahler-minimizer-compositum entry). It entered mathematics from architecture: Dom Hans van der Laan introduced it (Le Nombre Plastique, 1960) as the ideal ratio of three-dimensional proportion — the same discovery made independently by Cordonnier — and Kruijtzer conjectured, and Aarts-Fokkink-Kruijtzer proved, that van der Laan's number is the only companion the golden ratio has. What "morphic" adds to the plastic number's distinctions is finality: the golden ratio's arithmetic of self-similarity, taken as a definition, has exactly one more solution among the reals. The formalized proof consumes Selmer's trinomial irreducibility theorem from Mathlib, derives the needed Tverberg-type instance through a mirror-dichotomy argument carried out entirely in the integer polynomial ring (simplifying the paper's complex-root analysis; disclosed in the fidelity block), and closes with the factorization endgame forcing (n, m) = (3, 5). No formalization of the morphic classification, the plastic number, or the Padovan/Perrin constants exists in any surveyed prover as of the 2026-09-01 sweep; Mathlib's golden-ratio development supplies one witness's vocabulary. Axioms on every compared theorem: propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound, audited in-build.

abstract: Kernel-checked entanglement package on the bipartite matrix algebra (2x2 tensor 2x2, native product index): (1) the separable-state CHSH bound 2 for the real-Pauli tuple, proved through the Bloch-disk constraint with no spectral theory; (2) an entanglement witness — a bipartite state, positive semidefinite with unit trace, that is NOT separable, with Born CHSH expectation equal to the Tsirelson value 2*sqrt(2) (the Bell state, exhibited explicitly in the Solution); (3) spectral projections without spectral theory — (1+W)/2 is an effect for every Hermitian involution W, any finite dimension; (4) the two-party correlation law forced, not postulated: for any state representing a generalized probability measure on effects (Busch's theorem vocabulary; no continuity assumed), the correlation at any pair of binary-observable settings is an explicit difference of the measure's values at two effects; (5) the assembly — a state that is not separable, is the UNIQUE state reproducing its own effect statistics (Born-rule uniqueness on the composite algebra), attains the Tsirelson value, and carries the witness correlation table XX = ZZ = 1, XZ = ZX = 0. Extended (second session, 2026-08-31) by five further compared theorems — the general bounds and the quantitative Werner-family layer: (6) the separable bound 2 at ARBITRARY finite local dimensions and arbitrary Hermitian-involution settings; (7) the state-level Tsirelson bound 2*sqrt(2) at the same generality; (8) the Werner family W_p = p|Phi+><Phi+| + ((1-p)/4)1, spelled inline from the explicit Bell projector, has CHSH expectation at most 2*sqrt(2)*p at any Hermitian-involution settings with traceless party-1 observables (p >= 0) — the Werner line of the Horodecki 1995 criterion; (9) the violation threshold: for p >= 0, W_p violates CHSH at some such settings iff p > 1/sqrt(2); (10) the separability endpoint (Werner 1989): W_p is separable for 0 <= p <= 1/3. All hypotheses are inline; the compared statements use only Mathlib vocabulary (Matrix.PosSemidef, Matrix.IsHermitian, Matrix.trace, the Kronecker product, Real.sqrt, Matrix.vecMulVec) with no custom definitions.

abstract: Kernel-checked proof of Busch's theorem in finite dimension: every generalized probability measure on the effects of a complex matrix algebra — nonnegative on effects, additive whenever a sum of effects is again an effect, normalized at the identity — is represented by a unique density matrix via the trace pairing. Existence and uniqueness are both compared (busch_representation). The result is the uniqueness of the Born rule in the POVM reading; it is valid in every finite dimension (beyond finiteness and decidable equality of the index type, the compared statement assumes only [Nonempty n]) and holds already at dimension 2, where Gleason's theorem (which requires dimension at least 3) does not apply. No continuity is assumed: for a normalized measure, nonnegativity plus additivity force real homogeneity on the effect interval (scalars in [0,1]), compared separately as homogeneity_automatic. The compared statements use only Mathlib vocabulary (Matrix.PosSemidef, Matrix.trace).

abstract: A Lean 4 formalization of the periodic Cooper-Wallis construction and of Hadamard existence at eight orders: from kernel-checked periodic T-matrix quadruples of orders 103 and 163 and seven symmetric-circulant Williamson quadruples, the development proves that Hadamard matrices of orders 2884, 4532, 7004, 7172, 7828, 8476, 9476, and 11948 exist. Each of the eight orders lands on an entry of Table 4 of Cati and Pasechnik's maintained construction database (arXiv:2411.18897v2, 2025-08-30) recording no Hadamard matrix of that order as known, and the source repositories' firsthand audit of the construction literature (closed 2026-08-29) located no published route to the order-103 or order-163 T-objects the eight are built from. The development also proves the erratum core of the companion Hadamard-M note on Miyamoto's 1991 construction paper: the handshake parity obstruction, its empty-class corollary, and the nonexistence of the displayed C2-matrix ingredient of that paper's Corollary 4 at every positive block order not congruent to 1 mod 4 - covering the paper's printed list entries at orders 103, 127, and 151 under both printed readings of the corollary's output order, and leaving the order-515 list entry, the paper's claim of a Hadamard matrix of order 2060, unsupported by the paper's own machinery. Cati and Pasechnik, for want of details, record being unable to verify the constructions claimed in that paper's section 7, naming order 4*515 as their example; the obstruction supplies an independent mathematical reason the printed route cannot deliver that entry. Order 2060 itself is not open: a Hadamard matrix of that order was posted publicly on 2026-08-23, credited to Schneider, by other means.

abstract: A Lean 4 formalization of an explicit construction for the Furstenberg-Sárközy problem. abstract: Kernel-checked exact-constant results for the CHSH operator T = A₀B₀ + A₀B₁ + A₁B₀ − A₁B₁ of an arbitrary CHSH tuple (Mathlib's IsCHSHTuple: self-adjoint involutions with the A's commuting with the B's). (1) The Landau identity: in any *-ring, T² = 4 + [A₀,A₁]·[B₁,B₀] — the exact, representation-independent correction to the naive T² = 8·1 (chsh_mul_self). (2) Tsirelson's bound in norm form: ‖T‖ ≤ 2√2 for every CHSH tuple in every nontrivial unital real C*-normed algebra (chsh_norm_le). (3) The classical constant, exactly: if either party's pair commutes, ‖T‖ = 2 — not merely ≤ 2 (chsh_norm_of_comm). (4) Necessity of noncommutativity: any violation ‖T‖ > 2 forces A₀A₁ ≠ A₁A₀ and B₀B₁ ≠ B₁B₀ — noncommutativity within both parties is necessary for any violation of the classical bound (noncomm_of_chsh_norm_gt_two). (5) The exact constant of M₄(ℝ): in the l2 operator norm, 2√2 is the greatest element of the set of CHSH operator norms over 4×4 real matrices — an upper bound for every tuple, attained by an explicit real-Pauli tuple (chsh_opNorm_isGreatest), so the maximal violation 2√2 is possible, not just bounded. The witness side stays compared: the explicit quadruple is verified to be a genuine CHSH tuple, its CHSH operator has eigenvalue exactly 2√2 on the explicit nonzero vector (1,0,0,1) and l2 operator norm exactly 2√2; the ordered star-ring bounds T ≤ (2√2)·1 and (commutative case) T ≤ 2 and the strict gap 2 < 2√2 complete the picture. A falsification is compared alongside: the saturating tuple's T² is not c·1 for ANY real c (chsh_sq_ne quantifies over every scalar), so the scalar-square route to the norm is closed for every scalar; the norm results here go through the C*-identity (and, for the generic bound, the Landau identity) instead.
